stages.note: New AWS accounts often have 0 vCPU for GPU instances. You file the request from your own AWS sign-in. Do not create the pool before the quota is 4 or more. You may prepare your cluster while you wait.

steps.h: Optional: ask your AI for GPU quota
steps.d: After your AWS account is connected, say: “Request AWS quota for one on-demand L4 or A10G GPU in us-east-1 for my connected account.” Your AI files the request through Multicloud only after the organization owner allows it: mctl cloud-account allow-quota-requests <cloud-account-id>. Without that, or if you prefer, run the commands below yourself.

The command prints one number: your vCPU limit for on-demand G and VT instances. 8 or more: skip the request. Less than 8: request 8 (one g6.2xlarge or g5.2xlarge needs 8; 4 fits only the smallest L4 or A10G size).
steps.c:
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-DB2E81BA \
  --region us-east-1 --query Quota.Value --output text

steps.d: 8 vCPU covers one g6.2xlarge (L4) or g5.2xlarge (A10G). 4 vCPU is the minimum.
steps.c:
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ec2 \
  --quota-code L-DB2E81BA --desired-value 8 --region us-east-1

steps.d: AWS can open a support case and ask for your use case. Reply: “Evaluation of LLM inference on one L4 or A10G GPU, on-demand, for about one week.”
This takes hours to a few days. CASE_OPENED or PENDING: wait. APPROVED: read your quota again with the first command; it must be 4 or more. DENIED: tell your Multicloud contact.
steps.c:
aws service-quotas list-requested-service-quota-change-history-by-quota \
  --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-DB2E81BA --region us-east-1 \
  --query 'RequestedQuotas[].[Status,DesiredValue,Created]' --output table
